paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Three days without water, and the people grumble. A few weeks later, empty stomachs, and they grumble again. But look who answers every time: the LORD. At Marah He sweetens the water, and He says, "I am the LORD who heals you" (Exodus 15:26). Then He rains down bread from heaven (Exodus 16:4). Moses even tells them the grumbling was "not against us but against the LORD" (Exodus 16:8), so the LORD is the One who hears every complaint.

The bread comes with a lesson in trusting Him. He tells them to gather enough for that day, and He says this is how He will test whether they follow His instructions (Exodus 16:4). Some people tried to keep leftovers anyway (Exodus 16:20). I get it, friend. I've watched a timer and still pulled the batch early, because I didn't trust the oven. But on the sixth day He gave them enough for two days, so they could rest on the Sabbath (Exodus 16:29). The LORD gave them what they needed, even a day off.

So what does that mean for you, baker? When you're in the desert, whether it's a bill, a long week or a plan that fell through, the LORD can take care of you one day at a time. Bring your needs to Him instead of grumbling about them. Moses cried out to the LORD at Marah (Exodus 15:25), and you can too. And remember that Aaron put a jar of manna before the LORD, "to be preserved for the generations to come" (Exodus 16:33), so everyone could remember how He fed His people.
